When adopting Prettier repo-wide (SYS-598) surfaced a conflict — CLAUDE.md mandated that all `@mantine/*` imports stay multi-line/one-specifier-per-line, but Prettier has no per-package import formatting concept and collapsed them to one line — the first instinct was to write a local ESLint autofix rule (mirroring the existing `local/require-use-client` pattern) to re-expand them after every Prettier run.

The user rejected this: "I think it would be simpler to drop the Mantine-specific rule and just let Prettier format the imports like any other."

**Why:** A custom rule fighting Prettier's own output is exactly the kind of "bespoke or idiosyncratic style" this project's SYS-598 ticket was trying to eliminate. Two tools each trying to own import formatting is fragile (order-dependent: prettier collapses, eslint --fix re-expands) and adds maintenance surface for a convention that wasn't load-bearing — it existed only to keep Mantine import diffs clean, a nice-to-have, not a correctness requirement like [[project_claim_page_no_home_link]]-style invariants.

**How to apply:** When a hand-written formatting convention conflicts with Prettier's actual output, default to relaxing the convention to match plain Prettier rather than building tooling to preserve the exception — unless the convention encodes a real invariant (e.g. `local/require-use-client`, which prevents a genuine RSC bug, not just a style preference). Ask before investing in a custom autofix rule for a cosmetic-only rule.

All test suites pass across every scoped layer (unit, services, components, actions, lib), plus typecheck, lint, format:check, and knip are all clean.

**Summary:**
- Added a `no-restricted-syntax` rule (`ImportSpecifier[importKind="type"]`) to `eslint.config.mjs`, replicated across the three overlapping rule blocks (base TS/TSX, runtime guardrails, App Router pages) since `no-restricted-syntax` arrays fully replace rather than merge — banning inline `type` modifiers so every type-only import must use a separate `import type {...}` statement, matching `consistent-type-imports`'s existing `fixStyle: 'separate-type-imports'`.
- Wrote a one-off TypeScript-compiler-API codemod to split all 40 files / 55 flagged imports it caught into separate statements, then ran `eslint --fix` (simple-import-sort resorted everything) and `npm run format` to normalize.
- Verified clean: typecheck, lint, format:check, knip, and full test suite (unit/services/components/actions/lib) all pass.

Changes are unstaged in the working tree, ready for you to review and commit.
